Fix \(P=P_{A,u,v}\in\mathcal P_n\).  The definition of \(\mathcal P_n\) gives \(\|u\|_2\le B\sqrt n\), \(\|v\|_2\le B\sqrt n\), and \(\|A^+\|_{\mathrm{op}}=s_r(A)^{-1}\le(cn)^{-1}\).  Therefore
\[
|\theta_n|=|uA^+v|
\le\|u\|_2\|A^+\|_{\mathrm{op}}\|v\|_2
\le\frac{B^2}{c}=M_0.
\tag{1}
\]
Thus the off-gate interval \([-M_0,M_0]\) always covers \(\theta_n\).

On \(G_n\), condition on \(X\).  By \(\textup{lem:conditional-reduction}\),
\[
Z_n=m_n+\xi_n,\qquad \xi_n\mid X\sim\mathcal N(0,I_{2r}),
\qquad
\theta_{X,n}=\sigma^2m_{p,n}^{\mathsf T}D_nm_{q,n},
\tag{2}
\]
and
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}
P\bigl(|\theta_{X,n}-\theta_n|>d_n,\,G_n\bigr)
\le e^{-n/2}+3(e+n)^{-6}.
\tag{3}
\]
The gate gives \(s_r(X)>0\), so every diagonal entry of \(D_n=\widehat S^{-1}\) is positive.  Applying \(\textup{lem:gaussian-outer-inversion}\) conditionally at this realized \(D_n\) and \(m_n\) yields
\[
P\left(
|\widehat\theta_n-\theta_{X,n}|>\sigma^2W_n
\,\middle|\,X\right)\le\alpha
\quad\hbox{on \(G_n\)}.
\tag{4}
\]
If neither failure in (3) and (4) occurs, the triangle inequality gives
\[
|\widehat\theta_n-\theta_n|
\le\sigma^2W_n+d_n,
\]
which is precisely on-gate membership of \(\theta_n\) in \(I_n^{\mathrm{out}}\).  Combining this fact with (1), integrating (4) over \(X\), and using (3),
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}P\{\theta_n\notin I_n^{\mathrm{out}}\}
\le\alpha+e^{-n/2}+3(e+n)^{-6}.
\tag{5}
\]
Taking the limit superior proves the asserted uniform coverage.  No step divides by \(u\), \(v\), or a loading norm.

For the comparison clause, \(\textup{prop:yan-wainwright-class-embedding}\) identifies \(\mathcal P_n\) with a canonical square one-target subclass satisfying Yan--Wainwright conditions \(4.1\)--\(4.4\mathrm b\) for sufficiently large \(n\).  The cited node \(\textup{lem:yan-wainwright-gaussian-condition}\) records that their Theorem~1 additionally assumes condition \(4.4\mathrm c\).  At \(u=v=0\), the law remains in \(\mathcal P_n\), (5) still applies, and the embedding proposition proves that condition \(4.4\mathrm c\) fails.  Hence the new coverage result includes joint-zero and arbitrarily slow loading transitions outside that loading-restricted theorem on the embedded subclass.  This argument neither identifies \(\mathcal P_n\) with, nor claims an extension over, the full published class.

Fix a sequence \(P_n\in\mathcal P_n\) with \(b_n/a_n\to0\).  In particular \(a_n>0\) eventually.  Write \(U_0=\|u\|_2\), \(V_0=\|v\|_2\), \(e_0=\|E\|_{\mathrm{op}}\), and
\[
a_{X,n}=\sigma^2s_D(m_n).
\tag{1}
\]
We first compare (1) with the population first-order scale.

On \(e_0\le cn/4\), let \(X_r=\widehat U\widehat S\widehat V^{\mathsf T}\).  The singular-vector equations, after projection onto the null complements of \(A\), give
\[
\|(I-UU^{\mathsf T})\widehat U\|_{\mathrm{op}}
+\|(I-VV^{\mathsf T})\widehat V\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\le K\frac{e_0}{n},
\qquad
\|\widehat S^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\frac{2}{cn}.
\tag{2}
\]
Indeed, \((I-UU^{\mathsf T})\widehat U\widehat S=(I-UU^{\mathsf T})E\widehat V\), and the retained singular values are at least \(cn-e_0\); the right-space equation is identical.  Put \(L=U^{\mathsf T}\widehat U\), \(M=V^{\mathsf T}\widehat V\), and \(B_X=U^{\mathsf T}X_rV=L\widehat S M^{\mathsf T}\).  Since the residual \(X-X_r\) is orthogonal to the retained left and right spaces, direct multiplication gives
\[
V^{\mathsf T}X_r^+U=(MM^{\mathsf T})B_X^{-1}(LL^{\mathsf T}).
\tag{3}
\]
The bounds in (2), the resolvent identity \(B_X^{-1}-S^{-1}=B_X^{-1}(S-B_X)S^{-1}\), and \(\|B_X^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le2/(cn)\) imply
\[
\|V^{\mathsf T}X_r^+U-S^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\le K\frac{e_0}{n^2}.
\tag{4}
\]
Decompose \(X_r^+U-A^+U\) into its projection onto \(\operatorname{col}(V)\) and its orthogonal complement.  Equation (4) controls the former; (2) and \(\|\widehat S^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le2/(cn)\) control the latter.  Transposition gives the second inequality below:
\[
\|(X_r^+-A^+)U\|_{\mathrm{op}}
+\|V^{\mathsf T}(X_r^+-A^+)\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\le K\frac{e_0}{n^2}.
\tag{5}
\]
The span assumptions give \(u=uVV^{\mathsf T}\) and \(v=UU^{\mathsf T}v\).  Therefore (5) and the reverse triangle inequality for Euclidean norms yield
\[
|a_{X,n}-a_n|
\le K\sigma\frac{e_0}{n^2}(U_0+V_0).
\tag{6}
\]
Moreover, since the singular values of \(A^+\) on its row and column spaces lie between \((C_0n)^{-1}\) and \((cn)^{-1}\),
\[
a_n\ge\frac{\sigma(U_0+V_0)}{\sqrt2C_0n}.
\tag{7}
\]

For completeness, a \(1/4\)-net argument gives \(e_0/n\to0\) in probability uniformly over the class.  A maximal \(1/4\)-separated unit-sphere net has at most \(9^n\) points, and
\[
P(e_0>x)\le2\,9^{2n}\exp\left(-\frac{x^2}{8\sigma^2}\right),
\tag{8}
\]
because \(\|E\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le2\max|x^{\mathsf T}Ey|\) over the two nets and each bilinear form is \(\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2)\).  Equations (6)--(8) prove
\[
\frac{a_{X,n}}{a_n}\longrightarrow1
\quad\hbox{in probability}.
\tag{9}
\]

The singular-value min--max formula implies \(|s_j(X)-s_j(A)|\le e_0\).  Hence, on \(e_0<cn/2\),
\[
\left|\frac{s_j(A)}{s_j(X)}-1\right|
\le\frac{e_0}{cn-e_0},
\qquad 1\le j\le r.
\]
Since \(r\le r_0\), this gives
\[
\frac{\sigma^2\|\widehat S^{-1}\|_{\mathrm F}}{b_n}
\longrightarrow1
\quad\hbox{in probability}.
\tag{10}
\]
Writing \(h_n=\|D_n\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\|\widehat S^{-1}\|_{\mathrm F}\), (9), (10), and \(b_n/a_n\to0\) imply
\[
\frac{s_D(m_n)}{h_n}
=\frac{a_{X,n}}{\sigma^2h_n}\longrightarrow\infty
\quad\hbox{in probability}.
\tag{11}
\]

Conditional on \(X\), \(\textup{lem:gaussian-outer-inversion}\) applies to the exact Gaussian experiment in \(\textup{lem:conditional-reduction}\).  Its every-sequence assertion and a subsequence argument applied to (11) give
\[
\frac{\sigma^2W_n}{z_\alpha a_{X,n}}\longrightarrow1
\quad\hbox{in probability on \(G_n\)},
\qquad z_\alpha=\Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha/2).
\tag{12}
\]
To justify the subsequence step, if (12) failed, one could choose realizations of \(X\) along a subsequence for which \(s_D(m_n)/h_n\to\infty\) but the conditional failure probability stayed bounded away from zero, contradicting the deterministic every-sequence conclusion of that lemma.

The expectation conclusion of \(\textup{lem:conditional-reduction}\), Markov's inequality, and \(w_n/a_n=1+b_n/a_n\to1\) give
\[
\frac{d_n\mathbf1\{G_n\}}{a_n}\longrightarrow0
\quad\hbox{in probability}.
\tag{13}
\]
Equation (8) and the strong-spectrum bounds imply \(P_n(G_n^c)\to0\).  On \(G_n\), the interval length is \(2\sigma^2W_n+2d_n\).  Combining (9), (12), and (13), and discarding the vanishing off-gate event, proves
\[
\frac{\operatorname{length}(I_n^{\mathrm{out}})}
{2\Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha/2)a_n}\longrightarrow1
\quad\hbox{in \(P_n\)-probability}.
\]
Only the divergence \(a_n/b_n\to\infty\) was used; no deterministic divergence rate or loading pretest was introduced.

Let \(r=1\), and write the retained singular triplet as \((\widehat u,\widehat s,\widehat v)\).  Direct substitution in the definitions gives the exact identity
\[
\widehat\theta_n
=\sigma^2Z_{p,n}^{\mathsf T}D_nZ_{q,n}
=\frac{(R\widehat v)(\widehat u^{\mathsf T}C)}{\widehat s}
=RX_r^+C.
\tag{1}
\]
Thus the center is exactly the rank-one four-block spectral plug-in center, independently of signs chosen for \(\widehat u\) and \(\widehat v\).  The observed first-order scale is
\[
\widehat a_{X,n}:=\sigma^2s_{Z,n}
=\sigma\left\{
\frac{(\widehat u^{\mathsf T}C)^2+(R\widehat v)^2}{\widehat s^2}
\right\}^{1/2},
\tag{2}
\]
which is the rank-one specialization of the Yan--Wainwright Gaussian variance formula in equations \(4.5\mathrm b\) and \(4.6\mathrm a\) of Yan and Wainwright~\cite{YanWainwright2024}.

Assume \(b_n/a_n\to0\).  With \(a_{X,n}=\sigma^2s_D(m_n)\), the scale comparison proved in \(\textup{thm:oracle-length}\) gives \(a_{X,n}/a_n\to1\) in probability.  Since \(Z_n=m_n+\xi_n\), the gradient map is \(h_n\)-Lipschitz and therefore
\[
|s_{Z,n}-s_D(m_n)|\le h_n\|\xi_n\|_2.
\tag{3}
\]
Here \(\|\xi_n\|_2=O_P(1)\), because its dimension is two, and
\[
\frac{\sigma^2h_n}{a_n}
\le\frac{\sigma^2\|\widehat S^{-1}\|_{\mathrm F}}{b_n}
\frac{b_n}{a_n}=o_P(1)
\tag{4}
\]
by the singular-value comparison in the proof of \(\textup{thm:oracle-length}\).  Equations (2)--(4) imply \(\widehat a_{X,n}/a_n\to1\).

Moreover \(t_{Z,n}=s_{Z,n}/h_n\to\infty\) in probability.  The definitions of \(R_{0,n},t_{-,n},t_{+,n}\) give
\[
R_{0,n}=O_P(\sqrt{\log(e+t_{Z,n})})=o_P(t_{Z,n}),
\quad
\frac{t_{\pm,n}}{t_{Z,n}}\to1,
\]
while \(\beta_\alpha(t_{-,n})\to0\), so \(\zeta_\alpha(t_{-,n})\to z_\alpha\).  Also \(\log(e+t_{+,n})/t_{Z,n}\to0\).  Substitution into the analytic half-width yields
\[
\sigma^2W_n=z_\alpha\widehat a_{X,n}+o_P(a_n).
\tag{5}
\]
Finally, the donor-allowance expectation bound in \(\textup{lem:conditional-reduction}\) and \(w_n/a_n\to1\) imply \(d_n=o_P(a_n)\).  Equations (1), (2), and (5) show that the center is the established rank-one spectral center and that the full on-gate half-width is the established Gaussian half-width plus \(o_P(a_n)\), as claimed.

Put \(\delta=2^{-p_n-1}\), let \(\mathcal B\) be the coordinate box of radius \(\delta\) about the exact dyadic arrays, and give every exact-dyadic public control radius zero.  We construct a coarse enclosure and a sharp enclosure.

Let \(T\) be a directed upper bound for every absolute coordinate on \(\mathcal B\).  At any point of \(\mathcal B\) on which the gate holds,
\[
\|X_r^+\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\frac{2}{cn},
\qquad
\|Z_{p,n}\|_2,\|Z_{q,n}\|_2\le\frac{\sqrt nT}{\sigma},
\qquad
t_{Z,n}\le\frac{\sqrt{2n}T}{\sigma}=:\overline t.
\tag{1}
\]
Because \(\beta_\alpha(t)=\alpha/[4(1+t)]\),
\[
0<\zeta_\alpha(t)\le z_{\max}:=\Phi^{-1}(1-3\alpha/8).
\tag{2}
\]
Set
\[
\overline R=\sqrt{C_{r,\alpha}\log(e+2\overline t+A_{r,\alpha})}
\]
and
\[
\overline W=\frac{2}{cn}
\left\{z_{\max}(\overline t+\overline R)
+\frac{C_{r,\alpha}}2\log(e+\overline t+\overline R)\right\}.
\tag{3}
\]
Monotonicity in the analytic-halfwidth formula gives \(W_n\le\overline W\).  In addition,
\[
|\widehat\theta_n|=|RX_r^+C|\le\frac{2T^2}{c},
\tag{4}
\]
and
\[
d_n\le K_0\sigma^2\ell_nn^{-2}
\left(\frac{\sqrt nT}{\sigma}+\sqrt{\ell_n}\right)^2=:\overline d.
\tag{5}
\]
Thus every feasible on-gate interval is contained in
\[
[-\overline H,\overline H],
\qquad
\overline H=\frac{2T^2}{c}+\sigma^2\overline W+\overline d,
\tag{6}
\]
and every off-gate interval equals \([-M_0,M_0]\).  Directed majorants of (1)--(6) are finite.  Using \(\log(e+x)\le1+x\) and \(\sqrt x\le1+x\) makes their magnitude exponents polynomially encodable even when their numerical values are large.  The hull of (6) and the fallback is therefore a computable enclosure without a spectral-gap premise.

For the sharp branch, put \(\tau=(cn/2)^2\) and define the invariant projectors
\[
P_R=\mathbf1_{(\tau,\infty)}(X^{\mathsf T}X),
\qquad
P_L=\mathbf1_{(\tau,\infty)}(XX^{\mathsf T}).
\tag{7}
\]
When their certified retained count is \(r\),
\[
X_r=P_LXP_R,
\qquad
X_r^+=X_r^{\mathsf T}(X_rX_r^{\mathsf T}+I-P_L)^{-1}.
\tag{8}
\]
To check (8), write \(X_r=U_rS_rV_r^{\mathsf T}\).  The inverse in (8) is \(U_rS_r^{-2}U_r^{\mathsf T}+I-P_L\), and multiplication by \(X_r^{\mathsf T}\) gives \(V_rS_r^{-1}U_r^{\mathsf T}\).

The corrected \(\textup{lem:certified-error-recurrence}\) supplies a polynomial-time Newton--Schulz candidate for the inverse in (8), tests its full directed residual, computes (7) by matrix-sign iteration, and adds
\[
\frac{2\chi^{2^j}}{1-\chi^{2^j}}
\tag{9}
\]
to the sign enclosure after \(j\) stages.  Its solved noncommutative recurrence controls both transported box error and rounding error.  A repeated singular value within the retained cluster changes an individual basis but not either projector.  A tie across the retained--discarded boundary is never accepted and invokes the coarse hull.

The exact interval is computed from the invariant formulas
\[
\widehat\theta_n=RX_r^+C,
\quad
s_{Z,n}=\frac1\sigma
\sqrt{\|X_r^+C\|_2^2+
\|(X_r^+)^{\mathsf T}R^{\mathsf T}\|_2^2},
\tag{10}
\]
\[
\|Z_{p,n}\|_2=\frac{\|P_RR^{\mathsf T}\|_2}{\sigma},
\qquad
\|Z_{q,n}\|_2=\frac{\|P_LC\|_2}{\sigma}.
\tag{11}
\]
Therefore the endpoints are invariant under every rotation within a repeated retained singular subspace.

It remains to certify the two quantiles.  Taylor's formula with integral remainder gives, for \(m\ge0\),
\[
\left|e^y-\sum_{j=0}^m\frac{y^j}{j!}\right|
\le\frac{e^{|y|}|y|^{m+1}}{(m+1)!}.
\tag{12}
\]
The identity
\[
\pi=16\arctan(1/5)-4\arctan(1/239)
\tag{13}
\]
and the alternating series for \(\arctan x\) give rational directed brackets for \(\pi\) with geometrically decreasing width.  Combining (12)--(13) with
\[
\Phi(x)=\frac12+\frac1{\sqrt{2\pi}}
\int_0^x e^{-t^2/2}\,dt
\tag{14}
\]
gives directed rational brackets for \(\Phi\).  For fixed \(r\),
\[
F_{\chi^2_{2r}}(x)
=1-e^{-x/2}\sum_{j=0}^{r-1}\frac{(x/2)^j}{j!},
\qquad x\ge0.
\tag{15}
\]
The standard-normal exponential moment follows by completing the square, so
\[
P(Z\ge x)\le\inf_{t>0}e^{-tx+t^2/2}=e^{-x^2/2}.
\tag{16}
\]
This gives a polynomial-bit normal-quantile bracket; (15) gives a bracket of size \(O_{r_0}(1+\log(1/\gamma))\) at upper-tail probability \(\gamma\).  On the finite interior brackets the densities are positive.  Directed probability bisection, retaining both branches whenever the function enclosure overlaps the target probability, returns a quantile enclosure \(Q\) of width at most
\[
8\cdot2^{1-q_n}(1+|Q|).
\tag{17}
\]
The series term counts, bisection counts, mantissa costs, and stored exponent lengths are polynomial in \(q_n,L_n,\lceil\log_2(1/\alpha)\rceil\), because \(r\le r_0\) is fixed.

At successively doubled precisions, attempt to certify that the entire box is off the gate or is on the gate with the common split (7).  The recurrence lemma gives a deterministic cap polynomial in \(n,L_n,p_n,\lceil\log_2(1/\alpha)\rceil\).  If neither comparison separates by the cap, return the coarse hull (6).  Hence the procedure terminates after logarithmically many attempts, each with polynomially many finite-precision matrix and scalar operations.

Fix \((X,R,C)\in\mathcal B\), write its exact interval as \([L,U]\), and write the returned interval as \([\underline L,\overline U]\).  The algebraic recurrences, residual test, sign tail (9), quantile brackets, and branch hull give
\[
\underline L\le L\le U\le\overline U.
\tag{18}
\]
By the definitions of the two accumulated propagation radii,
\[
0\le L-\underline L\le\Delta_n^{\mathrm{enc}}+\Delta_n^{\mathrm{arith}},
\qquad
0\le\overline U-U\le\Delta_n^{\mathrm{enc}}+\Delta_n^{\mathrm{arith}}.
\tag{19}
\]
Adding (19) proves the stated factor-two length bound.  Arbitrary-precision signed exponents exclude overflow and subnormal values in the abstract model.  An IEEE backend emits no certificate unless exact power-of-two rescaling and exponent widening exclude overflow, subnormals, and flushing.  This proves all claims for exact-dyadic controls.  A refinable-control corollary needs the additional uniform modulus stated in the narrowed theorem, and no such modulus is silently assumed here.

First, the schedule and the definition of \(T_n^{\mathrm{enc}}\) give, when \(C_\star\ge4\),
\[
T_n^{\mathrm{enc}}
=2^{L_n-p_n-\lceil\log_2(p_n+2)\rceil-4}
=2^{\lceil\log_2\tau_n\rceil+2g_n+C_\star-4}
\ge\tau_n.
\tag{1}
\]
Also \(p_n,q_n,L_n\) are polynomially bounded in \(n\) and \(h_\alpha\).  On \(\kappa_n=0\), each rounded coordinate has numerator length at most
\[
p_n+\lceil\log_2(T_n^{\mathrm{enc}}+1)\rceil+2,
\]
and its signed exponent \(-p_n\) has \(O(\log(p_n+2))\) bits.  A sufficiently large fixed \(C_\star\), together with the theorem's exact-dyadic control-length premise, therefore places every input in \(\mathbb D_{L_n}\) and in the directed-arithmetic model.

There are \(N_n=n^2+2n\le3n^2\) observed coordinates, and every mean coordinate is bounded by \(B\).  Completing the square in the standard-normal moment generating function and applying exponential Markov inequality gives
\[
P(|Z|>x)\le2e^{-x^2/2},
\qquad x\ge0.
\tag{2}
\]
Since (1) gives \(T_n^{\mathrm{enc}}\ge B+\sigma\sqrt{12\log(e+n)}+1\), a union bound yields
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}P(\kappa_n=1)
\le2N_ne^{-6\log(e+n)}
\le6n^2(e+n)^{-6}=O(n^{-4})=o(n^{-1}).
\tag{3}
\]

We next isolate the stable donor event.  A maximal \(1/4\)-separated subset of the Euclidean unit sphere has at most \(9^n\) points, by comparing the disjoint radius-\(1/8\) balls with the radius-\(9/8\) ball.  Approximation of both unit vectors by such nets gives \(\|E\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le2\max|x^{\mathsf T}Ey|\).  Each \(x^{\mathsf T}Ey/\sigma\) is standard normal.  Thus (2) and a union bound imply, for a fixed \(k_0>0\) and all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}
P\{\|E\|_{\mathrm{op}}>cn/8\}
\le2\,9^{2n}\exp\left(-\frac{c^2n^2}{512\sigma^2}\right)
\le e^{-k_0n^2}.
\tag{4}
\]
For any matrices \(M,H\), the singular-value variational formula and the triangle inequality give \(|s_j(M+H)-s_j(M)|\le\|H\|_{\mathrm{op}}\).  Hence, off the event in (4), exact rank and strong spectrum imply
\[
s_r(X)\ge7cn/8,\qquad s_{r+1}(X)\le cn/8,\qquad
s_1(X)\le C_0n+cn/8.
\tag{5}
\]
The true donor and every point in its encoding box differ entrywise by at most \(2^{-p_n}\), hence in operator norm by at most \(n2^{-p_n}\).  For all sufficiently large \(n\), every donor in that box therefore satisfies
\[
s_r\ge3cn/4,\qquad s_{r+1}\le cn/4,\qquad
s_1\le3C_0n/2.
\tag{6}
\]

Put
\[
\mathcal H_n=n+T_n^{\mathrm{enc}}+\alpha^{-1}+p_n+q_n+1,
\qquad
P_n^\star=K_\star\mathcal H_n^{k_\star}.
\]
For fixed \(\alpha\) and fixed class constants, (1) and the definition of \(g_n\) show that \(T_n^{\mathrm{enc}}\), \(\mathcal H_n\), and \(P_n^\star\) are polynomial in \(n\).  On \(\kappa_n=0\), the coordinate box is bounded by \(T_n^{\mathrm{enc}}+1\).  Apply the two branches of \(\textup{lem:stable-certified-padding}\), using (4)--(6):
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}\mathbb E_P[&
(\Delta_n^{\mathrm{enc}}+\Delta_n^{\mathrm{arith}})
\mathbf1\{\kappa_n=0\}]\\
&\le P_n^\star(2^{-p_n}+2^{1-q_n})
+P_n^\star e^{-k_0n^2}
=o(n^{-m})
\end{aligned}
\tag{7}
\]
for every fixed \(m>0\).  Here \(p_n=n^2+4g_n\) and \(q_n=n^2+3g_n\).  Since every recorded radius is nonnegative, (7) also bounds each individual summand.

The corrected deterministic certificate applies because every public control is exact dyadic.  On \(\kappa_n=0\), it gives
\[
I_n^{\mathrm{out}}(X,R,C)\subseteq I_n^{\mathrm{fp}},
\qquad
0\le\varepsilon_n
\le2(\Delta_n^{\mathrm{enc}}+\Delta_n^{\mathrm{arith}})
=2\Delta_n^{\mathrm{num}}.
\tag{8}
\]
On \(\kappa_n=1\), the composed procedure returns \([-M_0,M_0]\).  This contains the target because
\[
|\theta_n|
\le\|u\|_2\|A^+\|_{\mathrm{op}}\|v\|_2
\le(B\sqrt n)\frac1{cn}(B\sqrt n)=M_0.
\tag{9}
\]
Also \(0\le\varepsilon_n\le2M_0\) on that branch.  Equations (3), (7), and (8) prove
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}\mathbb E_P[\varepsilon_n]=o(n^{-1}),
\qquad
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}
\mathbb E_P[M_0\mathbf1\{\kappa_n=1\}]=o(n^{-1}),
\tag{10}
\]
and the same \(o(n^{-1})\) bound for every recorded summand.

Equations (8)--(9) imply pointwise that coverage by \(I_n^{\mathrm{out}}\) entails coverage by \(I_n^{\mathrm{fp}}\), while the exceptional branch always covers.  The proved \(\textup{thm:uniform-coverage}\) therefore yields
\[
\liminf_n\inf_{P\in\mathcal P_n}
P\{\theta_n\in I_n^{\mathrm{fp}}\}\ge1-\alpha.
\tag{11}
\]
Furthermore,
\[
w_n\ge b_n=\sigma^2\|A^+\|_{\mathrm F}
\ge\frac{\sigma^2}{s_1(A)}
\ge\frac{\sigma^2}{C_0n}.
\tag{12}
\]
Combining (10)--(12) gives
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}
\frac{\mathbb E_P[\varepsilon_n]}{w_n}\longrightarrow0.
\tag{13}
\]
For nonnegative \(x,y\), \(x\le y+[x-y]_+\), so
\[
\operatorname{length}(I_n^{\mathrm{fp}})
\le\operatorname{length}(I_n^{\mathrm{out}})+\varepsilon_n.
\]
The established \(\textup{thm:transition-length}\) and (13) prove the asserted transition-order expected-length bound.

Finally, suppose \(b_n/a_n\to0\).  Equation (12) implies
\[
na_n\ge\frac{\sigma^2}{C_0}\frac{a_n}{b_n}\longrightarrow\infty.
\tag{14}
\]
From (10) and (14),
\[
\frac{\mathbb E_{P_n}[\varepsilon_n]}{a_n}
=\frac{n\mathbb E_{P_n}[\varepsilon_n]}{na_n}\longrightarrow0.
\tag{15}
\]
Thus \(\varepsilon_n/a_n\to0\) in \(L^1(P_n)\) and in probability.  On \(\kappa_n=0\), (8) makes the length difference nonnegative and at most \(\varepsilon_n\); on \(\kappa_n=1\), its probability vanishes by (3).  Therefore
\[
\frac{\operatorname{length}(I_n^{\mathrm{fp}})
-\operatorname{length}(I_n^{\mathrm{out}})}{a_n}
\longrightarrow0
\quad\hbox{in probability}.
\tag{16}
\]
The proved \(\textup{thm:oracle-length}\), followed by (16), yields the stated oracle Gaussian ratio.  The uniform summand bounds in (10) already imply the advertised \(o(n^{-1})\) conclusion at \(r=1,u=v=0\), where \(b_n\) itself is of order \(n^{-1}\).  This completes the affirmative resolution under exact-dyadic public controls.

Fix \(P=P_{A,u,v}\in\mathcal P_n\), and write the compact singular-value decomposition
\[
A=USV^{\mathsf T},
\qquad cn\le s_r(A)\le s_1(A)\le C_0n.
\tag{1}
\]
The span conditions give \(u=uVV^{\mathsf T}\) and \(v=UU^{\mathsf T}v\).  Define
\[
\ell=S^{-1}V^{\mathsf T}u^{\mathsf T},\qquad
q=S^{-1}U^{\mathsf T}v,\qquad
L=\begin{bmatrix}U\\ \ell^{\mathsf T}\end{bmatrix},\qquad
H=\begin{bmatrix}V\\ q^{\mathsf T}\end{bmatrix}.
\]
Then block multiplication and the definition of \(\theta_n\) give
\[
LSH^{\mathsf T}
=\begin{bmatrix}
A&UU^{\mathsf T}v\\
uVV^{\mathsf T}&uVS^{-1}U^{\mathsf T}v
\end{bmatrix}
=\begin{bmatrix}A&v\\u&\theta_n\end{bmatrix}
=\overline M_n.
\tag{2}
\]
The first \(n\) rows of \(L\) and \(H\) are \(U\) and \(V\), so both factors have column rank \(r\).  Since \(S\) is invertible, (2) proves \(\operatorname{rank}(\overline M_n)=r\).  The Gaussian-block assumption says that the three observed blocks have means \((A,v,u)\), observations \((X,C,R)\), and mutually independent \(\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2)\) entry noise.  The lower-right scalar is missing.  Thus this is the four-block model with \(N=T=n+1\), \(N_1=T_1=n\), and \(N_2=T_2=1\).  Its mean entries are bounded by \(\max\{B,B^2/c\}\), by (1) and the calculation in (1) of the coverage proof.

We verify the conditions in equations \(4.1\)--\(4.4\) of Yan and Wainwright~\cite{YanWainwright2024}.  The entry bound and (1) imply
\[
\|\ell\|_2\le\frac{\|u\|_2}{s_r(A)}
\le\frac{B}{c\sqrt n},
\qquad
\|q\|_2\le\frac{B}{c\sqrt n}.
\tag{3}
\]
An orthonormal basis of \(\operatorname{col}(L)\) is \(\overline U=L(L^{\mathsf T}L)^{-1/2}O_L\), for an orthogonal \(O_L\).  If \(\overline U_1\) denotes its first \(n\) rows, then
\[
\overline U_1^{\mathsf T}\overline U_1
=O_L^{\mathsf T}(I_r+\ell\ell^{\mathsf T})^{-1}O_L.
\tag{4}
\]
For all sufficiently large \(n\), (3)--(4) give
\[
\frac12 I_r\preceq\overline U_1^{\mathsf T}\overline U_1\preceq I_r.
\tag{5}
\]
The identical calculation for \(H\) gives (5) for \(\overline V_1\).  Since \(n/(n+1)\in[1/2,1]\), condition \(4.1\) holds, for example with fixed constants \(c_\ell=1/2\) and \(c_u=2\).

Deleting the last row and column is multiplication by coordinate contractions.  The singular-value variational formula therefore gives
\[
\sigma_r^\star=s_r(\overline M_n)\ge s_r(A)\ge cn.
\tag{6}
\]
Yan--Wainwright scale each noise entry to have variance \(\omega^2/(NT)\).  Here the variance is \(\sigma^2\) and \(N=T=n+1\), so the correct normalization is
\[
\omega=\sigma\sqrt{NT}=\sigma(n+1).
\tag{7}
\]
Consequently their global quantity in condition \(4.2\) satisfies
\[
\rho_{N,T}
=\frac{\omega}{\sigma_r^\star\sqrt{\min\{N_1,T_1\}}}
\le\frac{\sigma(n+1)}{cn\sqrt n}=O(n^{-1/2}),
\tag{8}
\]
and \(\min\{N_1,T_1\}=n\) eventually exceeds every fixed multiple of \(\log(N+T)\).  Since \(r\le r_0\),
\[
\rho_{N,T}\sqrt{r+\log(N+T)}
=O\left(\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n}}\right)\longrightarrow0,
\tag{9}
\]
which verifies condition \(4.3\) for every fixed positive approximation tolerance.

The local quantities in condition \(4.4\) use the entrywise noise standard deviation \(\omega/\sqrt{NT}=\sigma\), not \(\omega\).  Hence
\[
\rho_N=\frac{\sigma}{\sigma_r^\star\sqrt{N_1}}
\le\frac{\sigma}{cn^{3/2}},
\qquad
\rho_T\le\frac{\sigma}{cn^{3/2}}.
\tag{10}
\]
The last row of \(\overline U\) has norm at most \(\|\ell\|_2\), and the last row of \(\overline V\) has norm at most \(\|q\|_2\).  Thus the target local incoherences in condition \(4.4\mathrm a\) satisfy
\[
\mu_{n+1}=\sqrt{\frac{n+1}{r}}
\|\overline U_{n+1,\boldsymbol\cdot}\|_2
\le\frac{\sqrt2B}{c},
\qquad
\nu_{n+1}\le\frac{\sqrt2B}{c}.
\tag{11}
\]
Combining (10)--(11), the two left sides of condition \(4.4\mathrm b\) are bounded, respectively, by
\[
\max\{\mu_{n+1}\rho_T,\nu_{n+1}\rho_N\}\sqrt r
\le\frac{\sqrt2B\sigma\sqrt{r_0}}{c^2n^{3/2}}\longrightarrow0
\tag{12}
\]
and
\[
\min\left\{\frac{\mu_{n+1}}{\sqrt{N_1}},
\frac{\nu_{n+1}}{\sqrt{T_1}}\right\}
\sqrt{r\log(N+T)}
\le\frac{\sqrt2B\sqrt{r_0\log(2n+2)}}{c\sqrt n}\longrightarrow0.
\tag{13}
\]
Thus conditions \(4.4\mathrm a\)--\(4.4\mathrm b\) hold uniformly for every fixed tolerance.

Finally, \(u=v=0\) satisfies every class condition.  Then \(\ell=q=0\), so \(\mu_{n+1}=\nu_{n+1}=0\), whereas \(\rho_N,\rho_T>0\).  With the extended-real convention for division by zero, the first factor in condition \(4.4\mathrm c\) is
\[
\min\left\{\frac{\rho_T}{\mu_{n+1}},
\frac{\rho_N}{\nu_{n+1}}\right\}=+\infty.
\]
Therefore condition \(4.4\mathrm c\) fails at joint zero.  Equations (1)--(13) prove precisely the canonical-subclass conclusion.  Notice in particular the corrected global order \(O(n^{-1/2})\) in (8) and the distinct local order \(O(n^{-3/2})\) in (10).

We first establish enclosure validity.  If \(\|x-\widehat x\|\le r(x)\) and \(\|y-\widehat y\|\le r(y)\), then the triangle inequality gives the stated addition rule.  Expanding
\[
xy-\widehat x\widehat y
=\widehat x(y-\widehat y)+(x-\widehat x)\widehat y
+(x-\widehat x)(y-\widehat y)
\tag{1}
\]
and using submultiplicativity gives the product rule before the nonnegative rounding term is added.  Correct directed rounding of a scalar result of magnitude at most \(2^{e_j}\) contributes at most \(2^{e_j-q_n}\); summing these contributions and using \(\|M\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\|M\|_{\mathrm F}\) gives the asserted normwise \(\omega_q\).  The mean-value theorem gives the scalar-function recurrence.

For a candidate inverse, put \(R=I-KL\).  The input enclosure implies
\[
\|R\|\le\|I-\widehat K L\|+r(K)\|L\|=\varrho(K,L)<1.
\tag{2}
\]
The finite identity \((I-R)\sum_{j=0}^{m-1}R^j=I-R^m\) and \(\|R^m\|\to0\) show
\[
(I-R)^{-1}=\sum_{j=0}^\infty R^j,
\qquad
\|(I-R)^{-1}-I\|\le\frac{\|R\|}{1-\|R\|}.
\tag{3}
\]
As \(KL=I-R\), equations (2)--(3) give
\[
\|K^{-1}-L\|
\le\frac{\|L\|\varrho(K,L)}{1-\varrho(K,L)},
\tag{4}
\]
which proves the residual-certified inverse radius.  The addition and inverse rules applied to \((S+S^{-1})/2\) prove the basic matrix-sign enclosure.  Induction over the finite directed computation graph now proves containment of every algebraic node.  Probability-bracketed bisection never discards a feasible quantile, and the hull of overlapping gate branches contains every feasible exact branch.

We next construct the inverse candidates and prove their cost.  For an invertible \(d\)-by-\(d\) center matrix \(K\), let
\[
\lambda=2^{-\lceil\log_2(\|K\|_1\|K\|_\infty)\rceil},
\quad L_0=\lambda K^{\mathsf T},
\quad L_{j+1}=L_j(2I-KL_j).
\tag{5}
\]
Since \(\|K\|_{\mathrm{op}}^2\le\|K\|_1\|K\|_\infty\), the eigenvalues of \(\lambda KK^{\mathsf T}\) lie in \((0,1]\), and
\[
\|I-KL_0\|_{\mathrm{op}}
=1-\lambda s_d(K)^2
\le1-\frac{s_d(K)^2}{2\|K\|_1\|K\|_\infty}.
\tag{6}
\]
Exact arithmetic gives
\[
I-KL_{j+1}=(I-KL_j)^2.
\tag{7}
\]
On every accepted computation node below, \(\|K\|_1\|K\|_\infty\le\mathcal H_n^d\) and \(s_d(K)^{-1}\le\mathcal H_n^d\) for a fixed \(d\).  Thus \(\delta_0:=\lambda s_d(K)^2\ge\mathcal H_n^{-d'}\) after increasing \(d'\).  Equations (6)--(7) make the exact residual at most \(1/8\) after
\[
J_{\mathrm{inv}}\le C\{\log\mathcal H_n+\log(q_n+2)\}
\tag{8}
\]
steps.  For rounded iterates, (1) gives, with \(\delta_{\mathrm{mach}}=C\mathcal H_n^d\epsilon_n^{\mathrm{mach}}\),
\[
\widehat r_{j+1}\le \widehat r_j^2
+\delta_{\mathrm{mach}}.
\tag{9}
\]
Let \(z_{j+1}=z_j^2\) with \(z_0=1-\delta_0\), and put \(d_j=[\widehat r_j-z_j]_+\).  While \(\widehat r_j\le1\), (9) gives
\[
d_{j+1}\le2d_j+d_j^2+\delta_{\mathrm{mach}}.
\]
Consequently, for the \(O(\log\mathcal H_n)\) steps needed to make \(z_j\le1/8\), induction gives \(d_j\le3^{j+1}\delta_{\mathrm{mach}}\le C\mathcal H_n^{d''}\epsilon_n^{\mathrm{mach}}\).  If the latter bound is at most \(1/8\), then \(\widehat r_j\le1/4\).  Thereafter (9) leaves \([0,1/3]\) invariant and drives the residual to \(O(\delta_{\mathrm{mach}})\).  Moreover \(L_j=K^{-1}(I-R_j)\) in exact arithmetic, so \(\|L_j\|\le2\|K^{-1}\|\) while \(\|R_j\|\le1\); applying (1) adds at most the already displayed polynomial perturbation to the rounded center.  The directed evaluation of (2) therefore certifies \(\varrho<1\) when \(C\mathcal H_n^{d''}\epsilon_n^{\mathrm{mach}}\le1/8\).  If this precision inequality fails, then \(1\le8C\mathcal H_n^{d''}\epsilon_n^{\mathrm{mach}}\), so any coarse radius bounded by \(C\mathcal H_n^d\) is also bounded by \(C\mathcal H_n^{d+d''}\epsilon_n^{\mathrm{mach}}\).  This proves both alternatives in the statement without assuming that a residual test succeeds at inadequate precision.

We now treat the invariant projectors quantitatively.  Put \(\tau=(cn/2)^2\).  On the stable box, the nonzero spectra of \(X^{\mathsf T}X-\tau I\) and \(XX^{\mathsf T}-\tau I\) are separated from zero by
\[
g_n^{\mathrm{sp}}
=\min\left\{(3cn/4)^2-(cn/2)^2,
(cn/2)^2-(cn/4)^2\right\}
=\frac{3c^2n^2}{16}.
\tag{10}
\]
Their norms are at most \(C n^2\).  Divide by a certified power of two between that upper bound and twice it.  The spectrum of the resulting symmetric matrix \(S_0\) lies in
\[
[-1,-\gamma]\cup[\gamma,1]
\tag{11}
\]
for a fixed \(\gamma>0\) depending only on \(c,C_0\).

For a scalar eigenvalue \(x\ne0\), put \(s=\operatorname{sign}(x)\) and \(z=(x-s)/(x+s)\).  Direct substitution in \(x^+=(x+x^{-1})/2\) gives
\[
\frac{x^+-s}{x^++s}=z^2.
\tag{12}
\]
Diagonalizing the symmetric \(S_0\) and applying (12) to each eigenvalue proves that the exact iterates satisfy
\[
\|S_j-\operatorname{sign}(S_0)\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\le\frac{2\chi^{2^j}}{1-\chi^{2^j}},
\qquad
\chi=\frac{1-\gamma}{1+\gamma}<1.
\tag{13}
\]
The quantity on the right is explicitly added to the returned sign, and hence projector, enclosure.  Taking \(J_{\mathrm{sign}}=O(\log(q_n+2))\) makes it at most \(2^{1-q_n}\).

It remains to control noncommuting rounded perturbations, which (13) alone does not do.  For \(F(S)=(S+S^{-1})/2\), the resolvent identity gives the exact expansion
\[
F(S+E)-F(S)
=\frac12(E-S^{-1}ES^{-1})
+\frac12S^{-1}ES^{-1}E(S+E)^{-1}.
\tag{14}
\]
Thus the Fr\'{e}chet derivative is \(DF_S(E)=\frac12(E-S^{-1}ES^{-1})\), with no commutativity assumption.  After the first exact sign step, every eigenvalue of \(S_j\) has absolute value at least one, so \(\|S_j^{-1}\|\le1\).  If \(e_j\) bounds the normwise difference between a rounded center and the corresponding exact iterate, (14), the inverse residual enclosure, and the transported rounding term yield
\[
e_{j+1}\le e_j+C e_j^2+C\mathcal H_n^d2^{1-q_n},
\qquad j\ge1.
\tag{15}
\]
The first step has the same form with a fixed constant depending on \(\gamma^{-1}\).  Put \(\Omega=C\mathcal H_n^d2^{1-q_n}\), let \(J=J_{\mathrm{sign}}\), and define \(\widetilde e_j=e_j+(J-j)\Omega\).  Then (15) implies
\[
\widetilde e_{j+1}\le \widetilde e_j+C\widetilde e_j^2.
\]
Since \(y+Cy^2\le y/(1-Cy)\) whenever \(Cy<1\), iteration gives, with \(x=e_1+J\Omega\),
\[
e_j\le\widetilde e_j\le\frac{x}{1-C(j-1)x},
\qquad 1\le j\le J,
\tag{16}
\]
whenever \(CJx<1\).  This is an explicit solution of the rounded perturbation recurrence.  The input box gives \(e_1\le C\mathcal H_n^d2^{-p_n}\), and \(J\le C\log(q_n+2)\le C\mathcal H_n\).  Therefore (16) is at most
\[
C\mathcal H_n^{d+2}
\bigl(2^{-p_n}+2^{1-q_n}\bigr)
\tag{17}
\]
when the precision is adequate.  When it is not, the same coarse-radius case split used after (9) gives (17) after increasing the exponent.  Equations (14)--(17) are the required solved noncommutative rounded-iterate recurrence.

The projectors are \((I\pm\operatorname{sign}(S_0))/2\).  On the stable box, (10), (13), and (17) certify the retained count and the gap.  Form
\[
X_r=P_LXP_R,
\qquad
K_r=X_rX_r^{\mathsf T}+I-P_L,
\qquad
X_r^+=X_r^{\mathsf T}K_r^{-1}.
\tag{18}
\]
The eigenvalues of \(K_r\) are the retained squared singular values and ones on the orthogonal complement.  Hence
\[
\|K_r\|\le C\mathcal H_n^2,\qquad
s_n(K_r)^{-1}\le1+(3cn/4)^{-2}\le2.
\tag{19}
\]
The Newton--Schulz construction (5)--(9) therefore produces and residual-certifies the inverse in (18); the product recurrence gives a polynomial-times-\(\epsilon_n^{\mathrm{mach}}\) pseudoinverse radius.  Only projectors appear, so repeated singular values within the retained cluster cause no division by an internal spectral gap.

All remaining centers are polynomially bounded.  In particular, orthogonal projection and the coordinate bound give
\[
\|Z_{p,n}\|_2,\|Z_{q,n}\|_2
\le\frac{\sqrt n(T_n^{\mathrm{enc}}+1)}{\sigma},
\qquad
\|D_n\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\frac{4}{3cn}.
\tag{20}
\]
The arguments of every logarithm and square root are at least one.  The normal tail probability used by \(\zeta_\alpha\) lies in \([3\alpha/8,\alpha/2]\); its density at the relevant quantile has reciprocal bounded by a polynomial in \(\alpha^{-1}\).  For fixed \(r\),
\[
1-F_{\chi^2_{2r}}(x)
=e^{-x/2}\sum_{j=0}^{r-1}\frac{(x/2)^j}{j!},
\tag{21}
\]
so at tail probability \(\alpha/[4(1+t)]\), both the quantile and the reciprocal density are polynomially bounded in \(\mathcal H_n\).  The scalar recurrence therefore transports every input and rounding radius by at most another fixed polynomial.

There are \(O(n^3)\) scalar operations per matrix product, the inverse and sign iteration counts are bounded by (8) and (13), and probability bisection takes \(O(q_n+\log\mathcal H_n)\) steps.  All center magnitudes are bounded by a fixed power of \(\mathcal H_n\), so stored exponents have \(O(\log\mathcal H_n)\) bits.  Standard integer multiplication at the stated mantissa lengths is polynomial-time.  Summing the transported errors over the polynomial computation graph, and using (9) and (17), proves separately
\[
\max_x\|\widehat x\|\le K_\star\mathcal H_n^{k_\star},
\qquad
\max_x r(x)\le K_\star\mathcal H_n^{k_\star}
\bigl(2^{-p_n}+2^{1-q_n}\bigr)
\tag{22}
\]
on the stable box.  The first inequality concerns centers and does not vanish with precision; the second concerns transported and final radii.  Outside the stable branch, the explicit coarse hull is polynomially bounded, and the inadequate-precision case split following (9) proves the claimed alternative radius bound.  This completes correctness, complexity, center control, radius control, and branching control.

On \(\kappa_n=0\), every point of \(\mathcal B_n\) has coordinate magnitude at most \(T_n^{\mathrm{enc}}+1\).  The gate implies, at every feasible on-gate point,
\[
\|X_r^+\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\frac{2}{cn},
\qquad
\|Z_{p,n}\|_2,\|Z_{q,n}\|_2
\le\frac{\sqrt n(T_n^{\mathrm{enc}}+1)}{\sigma}.
\tag{1}
\]
Consequently the center, analytic half-width, donor allowance, and every feasible on-gate endpoint are bounded by a fixed polynomial in \(\mathcal H_n=n+T_n^{\mathrm{enc}}+\alpha^{-1}+p_n+q_n+1\).  The off-gate interval has fixed radius \(M_0=B^2/c\).  Hence the hull of all feasible branches is contained in \([-K\mathcal H_n^k,K\mathcal H_n^k]\).  The certified handle may stop at that hull, so
\[
0\le\Delta_n^{\mathrm{enc}}+\Delta_n^{\mathrm{arith}}
\le K\mathcal H_n^k.
\tag{2}
\]
Exact-dyadic public controls have input radius zero.

Now assume the three stable spectral inequalities.  With \(\tau=(cn/2)^2\), the retained and discarded squared singular values are separated from \(\tau\) by at least
\[
\min\left\{(3cn/4)^2-(cn/2)^2,
(cn/2)^2-(cn/4)^2\right\}
=\frac{3c^2n^2}{16}.
\tag{3}
\]
The corrected \(\textup{lem:certified-error-recurrence}\) applies.  Its Newton--Schulz residual construction, explicit matrix-sign tail, noncommutative recurrence, and scalar propagation prove that the sharp branch is certified whenever the precision inequality in that lemma holds, and then
\[
\Delta_n^{\mathrm{enc}}+\Delta_n^{\mathrm{arith}}
\le K\mathcal H_n^k(2^{-p_n}+2^{1-q_n}).
\tag{4}
\]
If that precision inequality fails, it says \(1\le K\mathcal H_n^d(2^{-p_n}+2^{1-q_n})\).  Multiplying (2) by this inequality and increasing the exponent gives (4) again.  Thus (4) holds without silently assuming adequate precision.  Every recorded summand is nonnegative and at most the displayed sum, which proves the final assertion.

theorem.statement:
Suppose the public controls \(\alpha,\sigma,c,C_0,B\) are exact dyadic inputs whose description lengths are eventually at most \(L_n\).  Put
\[
h_\alpha=\lceil\log_2(64/\alpha)\rceil,
\qquad
g_n=20\{h_\alpha+\lceil\log_2(n+2)\rceil+1\},
\]
\[
p_n=n^2+4g_n,\qquad q_n=p_n-g_n,\qquad
\tau_n=B+\sigma\sqrt{12\log(e+n)}+1,
\]
and, for a sufficiently large fixed integer \(C_\star\),
\[
L_n=p_n+\lceil\log_2(p_n+2)\rceil
+\lceil\log_2\tau_n\rceil+2g_n+C_\star.
\]
Then \(p_n,L_n,q_n\) are polynomially bounded in \(n\) and \(\lceil\log_2(1/\alpha)\rceil\), \(T_n^{\mathrm{enc}}\ge\tau_n\), and the composed measurable interval \(I_n^{\mathrm{fp}}\) satisfies
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{P\in\mathcal P_n}
P\{\theta_n\in I_n^{\mathrm{fp}}\}\ge1-\alpha,
\qquad
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}P(\kappa_n=1)=o(n^{-1}),
\]
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}
\frac{\mathbb E_P[\varepsilon_n]}{w_n}\longrightarrow0,
\qquad
\limsup_{n\to\infty}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}
\frac{\mathbb E_P[\operatorname{length}(I_n^{\mathrm{fp}})]}{w_n}
\le K_\alpha.
\]
On \(\kappa_n=0\),
\[
I_n^{\mathrm{out}}(X,R,C)\subseteq I_n^{\mathrm{fp}},
\qquad
0\le\varepsilon_n\le2\Delta_n^{\mathrm{num}};
\]
on \(\kappa_n=1\), \(I_n^{\mathrm{fp}}=[-M_0,M_0]\).  Along every sequence \(P_n\in\mathcal P_n\) with \(b_n/a_n\to0\),
\[
\frac{\varepsilon_n}{a_n}\longrightarrow0
\quad\hbox{in \(L^1(P_n)\) and in probability},
\qquad
\frac{\operatorname{length}(I_n^{\mathrm{fp}})}
{2\Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha/2)a_n}\longrightarrow1
\quad\hbox{in probability}.
\]
Finally, uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal P_n\), the expectation of every nonnegative recorded summand of \(\Delta_n^{\mathrm{enc}}\) and \(\Delta_n^{\mathrm{arith}}\), the fallback contribution \(M_0\mathbf1\{\kappa_n=1\}\), and \(\varepsilon_n\) is \(o(n^{-1})\).  In particular, this holds along every sequence with \(r=1\) and \(u=v=0\).
theorem.proof_tex:
First, the schedule and the definition of \(T_n^{\mathrm{enc}}\) give, when \(C_\star\ge4\),
\[
T_n^{\mathrm{enc}}
=2^{L_n-p_n-\lceil\log_2(p_n+2)\rceil-4}
=2^{\lceil\log_2\tau_n\rceil+2g_n+C_\star-4}
\ge\tau_n.
\tag{1}
\]
Also \(p_n,q_n,L_n\) are polynomially bounded in \(n\) and \(h_\alpha\).  On \(\kappa_n=0\), each rounded coordinate has numerator length at most
\[
p_n+\lceil\log_2(T_n^{\mathrm{enc}}+1)\rceil+2,
\]
and its signed exponent \(-p_n\) has \(O(\log(p_n+2))\) bits.  A sufficiently large fixed \(C_\star\), together with the theorem's exact-dyadic control-length premise, therefore places every input in \(\mathbb D_{L_n}\) and in the directed-arithmetic model.

There are \(N_n=n^2+2n\le3n^2\) observed coordinates, and every mean coordinate is bounded by \(B\).  Completing the square in the standard-normal moment generating function and applying exponential Markov inequality gives
\[
P(|Z|>x)\le2e^{-x^2/2},
\qquad x\ge0.
\tag{2}
\]
Since (1) gives \(T_n^{\mathrm{enc}}\ge B+\sigma\sqrt{12\log(e+n)}+1\), a union bound yields
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}P(\kappa_n=1)
\le2N_ne^{-6\log(e+n)}
\le6n^2(e+n)^{-6}=O(n^{-4})=o(n^{-1}).
\tag{3}
\]

We next isolate the stable donor event.  A maximal \(1/4\)-separated subset of the Euclidean unit sphere has at most \(9^n\) points, by comparing the disjoint radius-\(1/8\) balls with the radius-\(9/8\) ball.  Approximation of both unit vectors by such nets gives \(\|E\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le2\max|x^{\mathsf T}Ey|\).  Each \(x^{\mathsf T}Ey/\sigma\) is standard normal.  Thus (2) and a union bound imply, for a fixed \(k_0>0\) and all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}
P\{\|E\|_{\mathrm{op}}>cn/8\}
\le2\,9^{2n}\exp\left(-\frac{c^2n^2}{512\sigma^2}\right)
\le e^{-k_0n^2}.
\tag{4}
\]
For any matrices \(M,H\), the singular-value variational formula and the triangle inequality give \(|s_j(M+H)-s_j(M)|\le\|H\|_{\mathrm{op}}\).  Hence, off the event in (4), exact rank and strong spectrum imply
\[
s_r(X)\ge7cn/8,\qquad s_{r+1}(X)\le cn/8,\qquad
s_1(X)\le C_0n+cn/8.
\tag{5}
\]
The true donor and every point in its encoding box differ entrywise by at most \(2^{-p_n}\), hence in operator norm by at most \(n2^{-p_n}\).  For all sufficiently large \(n\), every donor in that box therefore satisfies
\[
s_r\ge3cn/4,\qquad s_{r+1}\le cn/4,\qquad
s_1\le3C_0n/2.
\tag{6}
\]

Put
\[
\mathcal H_n=n+T_n^{\mathrm{enc}}+\alpha^{-1}+p_n+q_n+1,
\qquad
P_n^\star=K_\star\mathcal H_n^{k_\star}.
\]
For fixed \(\alpha\) and fixed class constants, (1) and the definition of \(g_n\) show that \(T_n^{\mathrm{enc}}\), \(\mathcal H_n\), and \(P_n^\star\) are polynomial in \(n\).  On \(\kappa_n=0\), the coordinate box is bounded by \(T_n^{\mathrm{enc}}+1\).  Apply the two branches of \(\textup{lem:stable-certified-padding}\), using (4)--(6):
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}\mathbb E_P[&
(\Delta_n^{\mathrm{enc}}+\Delta_n^{\mathrm{arith}})
